"**Not Like Us** " is a [diss track](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diss_track "Diss track") by the American rapper [Kendrick Lamar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kendrick_Lamar "Kendrick Lamar") released amidst [his highly publicized feud](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake%E2%80%93Kendrick_Lamar_feud "Drake–Kendrick Lamar feud") with the Canadian rapper [Drake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\) "Drake \(musician\)"). It was released on May 4, 2024, through [Interscope Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interscope_Records "Interscope Records"), less than 20 hours after Lamar's previous diss track "[Meet the Grahams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meet_the_Grahams "Meet the Grahams")". A [music video](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_video "Music video"), directed by [Dave Free](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dave_Free "Dave Free") and Lamar, was released on [American Independence Day](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Independence_Day_\(United_States\) "Independence Day \(United States\)") (July 4).
Primarily produced by [Mustard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mustard_\(music_producer\) "Mustard \(music producer\)"), with additional work from [Sounwave](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sounwave "Sounwave") and [Sean Momberger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Momberger "Sean Momberger"), "Not Like Us" is a [hyphy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hyphy "Hyphy")-influenced [West Coast hip-hop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Coast_hip-hop "West Coast hip-hop") song with a prominent [bassline](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bassline "Bassline"), lively [strings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/String_\(music\) "String \(music\)"), and [finger snaps](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Finger_snapping "Finger snapping"). Lyrically, it continues the themes introduced in "Meet the Grahams". Lamar doubles down on allegations of Drake's [sexual interest in minors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pedophilia "Pedophilia") and [sexual misconduct](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sexual_misconduct "Sexual misconduct"). He also criticizes his [cultural identity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cultural_identity "Cultural identity") and relationships with [artists based](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_of_Atlanta "Music of Atlanta") in [Atlanta, Georgia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atlanta "Atlanta"), accusing him of exploiting them for [street credibility](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Street_credibility "Street credibility") and financial gain.
"Not Like Us" received acclaim from critics, who praised the production, songwriting, and Lamar's performance; they felt it solidified Lamar's victory, and is widely regarded as the feud's best track. "Not Like Us" broke numerous records on the streaming platform [Spotify](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spotify "Spotify") and peaked at number one in ten countries, while charting in the top ten in over 20 additional countries. Drake responded to "Not Like Us" with "[The Heart Part 6](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Heart_Part_6 "The Heart Part 6")", in which he denied Lamar's accusations, on May 5. In January 2025, Drake filed a lawsuit against Interscope's parent [Universal Music Group](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Universal_Music_Group "Universal Music Group") (UMG), alleging that "Not Like Us" [defamed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Defamation "Defamation") him and that UMG and Spotify artificially inflated its popularity; the lawsuit was dismissed in October 2025.
"Not Like Us" won all five of its [Grammy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Awards "Grammy Awards") nominations at the [67th ceremony](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/67th_Annual_Grammy_Awards "67th Annual Grammy Awards"): [Record of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Record_of_the_Year "Grammy Award for Record of the Year"), [Song of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Song_of_the_Year "Grammy Award for Song of the Year"), [Best Rap Performance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Best_Rap_Performance "Grammy Award for Best Rap Performance"), [Best Rap Song](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Best_Rap_Song "Grammy Award for Best Rap Song"), and [Best Music Video](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Best_Music_Video "Grammy Award for Best Music Video"). It is tied with [the 5th Dimension](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_5th_Dimension "The 5th Dimension")'s "[Up, Up and Away](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Up,_Up_and_Away_\(song\) "Up, Up and Away \(song\)")" as the most-awarded song in Grammy history. Lamar first performed "Not Like Us" live on [Juneteenth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juneteenth "Juneteenth") 2024 during [The Pop Out: Ken & Friends](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Pop_Out:_Ken_&_Friends "The Pop Out: Ken & Friends"), where he played it five consecutive times. He performed it when he headlined the [Super Bowl LIX halftime show](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_LIX_halftime_show "Super Bowl LIX halftime show") in February 2025 and throughout his [Grand National Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand_National_Tour "Grand National Tour") from April to October 2025.
## Background and release
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Not_Like_Us&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Background and release")]
Further information: [Drake–Kendrick Lamar feud](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake%E2%80%93Kendrick_Lamar_feud "Drake–Kendrick Lamar feud")
American rapper [Kendrick Lamar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kendrick_Lamar "Kendrick Lamar") and Canadian rapper [Drake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\) "Drake \(musician\)") have been engaged in a [rap feud](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake%E2%80%93Kendrick_Lamar_feud "Drake–Kendrick Lamar feud") since August 2013.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-:3-1) Tensions escalated in March 2024, following Lamar's surprise appearance on [Future](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Future_\(rapper\) "Future \(rapper\)") and [Metro Boomin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metro_Boomin "Metro Boomin")'s single "[Like That](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Like_That_\(Future,_Metro_Boomin_and_Kendrick_Lamar_song\) "Like That \(Future, Metro Boomin and Kendrick Lamar song\)")", which was perceived as a diss aimed at Drake and [J. Cole](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/J._Cole "J. Cole") over their track "[First Person Shooter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_Person_Shooter_\(song\) "First Person Shooter \(song\)")".[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-:3-1) Drake responded to Lamar's verse with the single "[Push Ups](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Push_Ups_\(song\) "Push Ups \(song\)")" and the since-removed song "[Taylor Made Freestyle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Made_Freestyle "Taylor Made Freestyle")".[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-:3-1) Lamar fired back with the songs "[Euphoria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euphoria_\(Kendrick_Lamar_song\) "Euphoria \(Kendrick Lamar song\)")" and "[6:16 in LA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/6:16_in_LA "6:16 in LA")".[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-:3-1)
Hours after "6:16 in LA" was released, Drake responded with the single "[Family Matters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Family_Matters_\(Drake_song\) "Family Matters \(Drake song\)")", in which he accused Lamar of [abusing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Domestic_violence "Domestic violence") his romantic partner, Whitney Alford, and alleged that one of his two children was fathered by his creative partner, [Dave Free](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dave_Free "Dave Free").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-:4-2) Less than an hour later, Lamar responded with "[Meet the Grahams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meet_the_Grahams "Meet the Grahams")", depicting Drake as an alleged [sexual predator](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sexual_predator "Sexual predator") who runs a [sex trafficking](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sex_trafficking "Sex trafficking") ring inside of his [Toronto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toronto "Toronto") mansion, known as the Embassy, while fathering a secret daughter.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-:4-2) "Not Like Us" was [unexpectedly released](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Surprise_album "Surprise album") on May 4, 2024, less than 24 hours after "Meet the Grahams" was published.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-3) The only prior marketing that the song received came from Anthony "Top Dawg" Tiffith, the head of Lamar's former record label [Top Dawg Entertainment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Top_Dawg_Entertainment "Top Dawg Entertainment"), who posted, "Dot, I see dead people" on [Twitter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twitter "Twitter") approximately two hours before its premiere.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-4)
Like Lamar's previous releases during the feud, "Not Like Us" was initially released as a [YouTube](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/YouTube "YouTube") exclusive before [Interscope Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interscope_Records "Interscope Records") serviced it to [music streaming platforms](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_streaming_service "Music streaming service") several hours later.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-New_diss-5) He reportedly removed the [copyright claims](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copyright "Copyright") for a limited time, effectively allowing the public to freely use the song even for commercial purposes.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-6) [Universal Music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Universal_Music_Group "Universal Music Group") promoted the song on [radio airplay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Airplay "Airplay") in Italy on May 10, 2024.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-Italy_airplay-7) A [blended](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mashup_\(music\) "Mashup \(music\)") version of the studio recording with the live performance from [the Pop Out: Ken & Friends](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Pop_Out:_Ken_&_Friends "The Pop Out: Ken & Friends") impacted radio stations in [California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/California "California") on July 11, 2024.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-California_radio-8)
### Cover art
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Not_Like_Us&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Cover art")]
The single's cover art shows a [bird's-eye view](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bird's-eye_view "Bird's-eye view") of Drake's Toronto mansion from a [Google Maps](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_Maps "Google Maps") [screenshot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Screenshot "Screenshot") with 13 red markers placed on its roof, symbolizing the presence of [registered sex offenders](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Registered_sex_offender "Registered sex offender").[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-Yet_another_diss-9) Following the song's release, the mansion's Google Maps view was vandalized, with users creating landmarks on the mansion with names such as "Owned by Kendrick", "Kendrick's dog" and "A-Minor". Neighboring houses were similarly vandalized, with titles such as "Zesty Drake", "CertifiedKidLover" and "ChildMOE-Lester". A forest near the mansion was renamed to "Money Trees", referencing [Lamar's 2012 song of the same name](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Money_Trees "Money Trees").[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-10)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-11)

Lamar accuses Drake of exploiting rappers through his relationships with [Future](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Future_\(rapper\) "Future \(rapper\)"), [Lil Baby](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Baby "Lil Baby"), [21 Savage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/21_Savage "21 Savage"), [Young Thug](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Young_Thug "Young Thug"), [Quavo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quavo "Quavo") and [2 Chainz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2_Chainz "2 Chainz") (clockwise from top left), all of whom hail [from or near Atlanta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atlanta_hip-hop "Atlanta hip-hop").
"Not Like Us" is a "[club](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nightclub "Nightclub")-friendly" [West Coast hip-hop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Coast_hip-hop "West Coast hip-hop") track with strong [hyphy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hyphy "Hyphy") stylings.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-Complete_lyrics-12) Several elements of its production, including the "stirring" [violins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Violin "Violin"), [piano](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Piano "Piano") and [brass instruments](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brass_instrument "Brass instrument"), were taken from [samples](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sampling_\(music\) "Sampling \(music\)") of [Monk Higgins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monk_Higgins "Monk Higgins")'s 1968 rendition of "I Believe to My Soul", a [cover](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cover_version "Cover version") of [Ray Charles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ray_Charles "Ray Charles")'s [1961 composition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Genius_Sings_the_Blues "The Genius Sings the Blues").[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-5_best_week-13) Despite speculation, the song does not include a sample of [Nas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nas "Nas")'s diss record "[Ether](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ether_\(song\) "Ether \(song\)")" (2001).[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-Mustard_beat-14) On "Not Like Us", Lamar employs a "comically exaggerated" [cadence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cadence "Cadence") that elicited comparisons to [Drakeo the Ruler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drakeo_the_Ruler "Drakeo the Ruler")'s signature [flow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rapping#Flow "Rapping").[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-15)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-16)

[Mustard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mustard_\(record_producer\) "Mustard \(record producer\)"), the song's primary producer, wanted to work with Lamar for years and would send him about five beats a day for three months.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-Kendrick_reaction-17) He was inspired to compose the beat after imagining what [Dr. Dre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dr._Dre "Dr. Dre") would create if he was in a recording studio with [Lil Jon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Jon "Lil Jon").[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-Mustard_beat-14) With contributions from [Sounwave](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sounwave "Sounwave") and Sean Momberger,[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-Mustard_beat-14) Mustard produced "Not Like Us" in about 30 minutes by speeding up the sample's [tempo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tempo "Tempo") to create a "relentless" and "urgent" atmosphere.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-Complete_lyrics-12) Its additional [bassline](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bassline "Bassline"), [snare drums](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Snare_drum "Snare drum"), and [finger snaps](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Finger_snapping "Finger snapping") heightened its "aggressive" tone.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-Breakdown-18) On April 6, 2024, Mustard sent the finished production to Lamar while attending his manager's birthday dinner.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-Kendrick_reaction-17) He received a complimentary [text message](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Text_messaging "Text messaging") from Lamar later that evening, but was unaware Lamar used it until the song came out.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-Kendrick_reaction-17)
### Lyrics
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Not_Like_Us&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Lyrics")]
"Not Like Us" begins with Lamar whispering "psst, I see dead people", a reference to _[The Sixth Sense](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Sixth_Sense "The Sixth Sense")_ (1999), which he previously referenced on "Euphoria".[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-19) Lamar then makes a series of allusions to his hometown of [Compton, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Compton,_California "Compton, California"), before accusing Drake of [sexual behavior with minors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ephebophilia "Ephebophilia").[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-Yet_another_diss-9)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-Breakdown-18) Lamar references Drake's album _[Certified Lover Boy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Certified_Lover_Boy "Certified Lover Boy")_ (2021) when labeling him and his label [OVO Sound](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/OVO_Sound "OVO Sound") as "certified pedophiles", specifically naming Chubbs, Drake's head of security; [PartyNextDoor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PartyNextDoor "PartyNextDoor"), the first artist signed; and [Baka Not Nice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baka_Not_Nice "Baka Not Nice"), who had been in prison for [human trafficking](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_trafficking "Human trafficking") before signing.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-20)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-:2-21)
Lamar also attacks Drake's personal relationships, alleging that Drake had sex with [Lil Wayne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Wayne "Lil Wayne")'s girlfriend, saying he "did [J.] Cole foul", and warning him to "not speak on Serena", referencing the fact that Drake and [Serena Williams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Serena_Williams "Serena Williams") – who also grew up near Compton – were romantically involved in 2015 and that Drake dissed [her husband](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alexis_Ohanian "Alexis Ohanian") in "[Middle of the Ocean](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Middle_of_the_Ocean "Middle of the Ocean")" (2022).[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-22)
Lamar challenges Drake's [cultural identity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cultural_identity "Cultural identity") throughout the track. In the second verse, Lamar accuses Drake of disrespecting the memory of rapper [2Pac](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tupac_Shakur "Tupac Shakur") by [artificially recreating](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence "Generative artificial intelligence") his voice on "Taylor Made Freestyle".[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-Breakdown-18) In the third verse, Lamar accuses Drake of exploiting [Black artists](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atlanta_hip-hop "Atlanta hip-hop") from [Atlanta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atlanta "Atlanta") for [street credibility](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Credibility#On_the_street "Credibility") and financial gain in the same way that [colonizers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colonization "Colonization") in the city exploited [slave labor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slave_labor "Slave labor"), using his collaborations with [Future](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Future_\(rapper\) "Future \(rapper\)"), [Lil Baby](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Baby "Lil Baby"), [21 Savage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/21_Savage "21 Savage"), [Young Thug](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Young_Thug "Young Thug"), [Quavo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quavo "Quavo"), and [2 Chainz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2_Chainz "2 Chainz") as examples.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-Yet_another_diss-9)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-:2-21)[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-23) The chorus, which consists solely of the phrase "they not like us", has been interpreted as a message that Drake and his associates "are unlike [Lamar's] own caliber, one that organically abides by the given morals of [Black culture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African-American_culture "African-American culture")".[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-24)
Lamar himself explained the personal meaning of the track in an interview with [SZA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SZA "SZA"):
> "Not Like Us" is the energy of who I am, the type of man I represent. Now, if you identify with the man that I represent … This man has morals, he has values, he believes in something, he stands on something. He’s not pandering.
> He’s a man who can recognize his mistakes and not be afraid to share the mistakes and can dig deep down into fear-based ideologies or experiences to be able to express them without feeling like he’s less of a man.
> If I’m thinking of "Not Like Us", I’m thinking of me and whoever identifies with that.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-25)
## Critical reception and analysis
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Not_Like_Us&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Critical reception and analysis")]
"Not Like Us" was met with widespread critical acclaim for the contagious production, Lamar's vocal performance, and scathing songwriting. _[GQ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GQ "GQ")_ 's Frazier Tharpe dubbed the track a leading contender for the "[song of the summer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Song_of_the_summer "Song of the summer")". He praised how the "banger" summoned Mustard's "raucous, party-starting homegrown energy" to deliver Lamar's "haymaker" that both out-strategized Drake and celebrated their West Coast upbringings.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-26) _[Stereogum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stereogum "Stereogum")_ editors found the song to be not only an "ultra-effective" diss record but a hit filled with "vicious" allegations and history lessons.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-5_best_week-13) Professional wrestler [Shawn Michaels](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Michaels "Shawn Michaels") appreciated that his _Sweet Chin Music_ [finisher](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glossary_of_professional_wrestling_terms#F "Glossary of professional wrestling terms") was mentioned in the song and invited Lamar and Drake to settle their differences at a _[WWE NXT](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WWE_NXT "WWE NXT")_ program.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-27)[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-28) Two other individuals referenced in the song, Serena Williams and [M. Night Shyamalan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/M._Night_Shyamalan "M. Night Shyamalan"), the writer and director of _[The Sixth Sense](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Sixth_Sense "The Sixth Sense")_ , praised it.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-29)[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-30) [Harvey Mason Jr.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harvey_Mason_Jr. "Harvey Mason Jr."), chief executive officer of [the Recording Academy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Recording_Academy "The Recording Academy"), praised the song's artistry and relevance.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-31)
Journalists described "Not Like Us" as a cultural touchstone, a [clarion call](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/clarion%20call "wiktionary:clarion call") for the West Coast, and one of the biggest diss tracks they have witnessed in their lifetimes.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-32)[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-BB5-33) They considered the timing of its release and content an effective strategy in capturing the [zeitgeist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zeitgeist "Zeitgeist") before listeners grew tired of the feud.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-BB5-33) Jordan Rose of _[Complex](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Complex_Networks "Complex Networks")_ declared "Not Like Us" as the best track released during Lamar and Drake's feud due to its electric tone and "contagious" production, although many of the lyrics are "very questionable". Rose believes that "time will tell" if the song marked the "end conclusion" of their war, but it has already proven itself to be "the stone that stunned [Goliath](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goliath "Goliath")."[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-34) _[Vibe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vibe_\(magazine\) "Vibe \(magazine\)")_ 's Armon Sadler ranked "Not Like Us" as the second-best track of the feud, praising the "undeniable bop" as a "masterclass" in execution.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-35) Mark Elibert from _[Billboard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_\(magazine\) "Billboard \(magazine\)")_ , who named it the fourth-best song, shared similar sentiments.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-36) Canadian outlets such as CBC News and _[Exclaim!](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Exclaim! "Exclaim!")_ opined that "Not Like Us" has grown into an [anti-Canadian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anti-Canadian_sentiment "Anti-Canadian sentiment") [anthem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthem "Anthem") reminiscent of "[Blame Canada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blame_Canada "Blame Canada")" from _[South Park: Bigger, Longer& Uncut](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Park:_Bigger,_Longer_&_Uncut "South Park: Bigger, Longer & Uncut")_ (1999).[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-37)[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-38) _[Uproxx](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uproxx "Uproxx")_ 's Wongo Okon noted it helped Lamar become a more appealing figure for [Generation Z](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generation_Z "Generation Z") and [Generation Alpha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generation_Alpha "Generation Alpha") listeners.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-39) _[Rolling Stone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rolling_Stone "Rolling Stone")_ 's Jeff Ihaza wrote in a two-year retrospective article that "the song's afterlife has been unusually protracted" and that it "changed the atmosphere around rap itself", noting that "The impression remains that [Drake] was beaten so badly that [he had to go to court to clear his name](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#Legal_actions)."[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-40)
The song has also been examined in the context of [race](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Race_\(human_categorization\) "Race \(human categorization\)") and [cultural appropriation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cultural_appropriation "Cultural appropriation"). [Salamishah Tillet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salamishah_Tillet "Salamishah Tillet") of _[The New York Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_New_York_Times "The New York Times")_ opined that while the message of "Not Like Us" may seem to attack Drake's [biracial](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multiracial_people "Multiracial people") identity, its popularity has inspired a broad assortment of [interracial interpretations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multiculturalism "Multiculturalism").[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-41) _Rolling Stone_ 's Andre Gee believes the song is a "rally against perpetrators who shifted hip-hop from a [Black](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_people "Black people") and [brown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brown_\(racial_classification\) "Brown \(racial classification\)") community with culturally understood modes of being into an at-times [parodic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parody "Parody") circus."[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-42) Mark P. Braboy of [The Triibe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Triibe "The Triibe") expanded on Gee's sentiments, applying the song's message to "culture vultures" in hip-hop journalism who have built their platforms by exploiting Black trauma.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-43)
_[Pitchfork](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pitchfork_\(website\) "Pitchfork \(website\)")_ named "Not Like Us" as the third-best song released in the [2020s](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020s_in_music "2020s in music") so far. In his accompanying excerpt, Alphonse Pierre declared the line "_Certified Lover Boy_? Certified pedophiles" as the "defining" lyric of the decade, in ways that are "unsettling and amazing and troubling and funny."[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-44) Other publications such as _Complex_ ,[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-45) _[HipHopDX](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HipHopDX "HipHopDX")_ ,[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-46) _[The Ringer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Ringer_\(website\) "The Ringer \(website\)")_ ,[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-47) and _[The Root](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Root_\(magazine\) "The Root \(magazine\)")_ ranked "Not Like Us" as one of the greatest diss tracks of all time.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-48)

## Commercial performance
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Not_Like_Us&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Commercial performance")]
### Global
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Not_Like_Us&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Global")]
"Not Like Us" was an immediate commercial success and broke numerous streaming records—most of which were previously held by Drake.[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-66) It led the [_Billboard_ Global 200](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Global_200 "Billboard Global 200") chart for four non-consecutive weeks, marking Lamar's first solo number-one song on the survey.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-67)[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-68) It is also reportedly the most-streamed diss track on [Spotify](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spotify "Spotify"),[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-:0-69) earning the biggest single-day streams for a hip hop song (12.8 million) and the most song streams in a week by a rapper (81.2 million).[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-70) Additionally, it became the fastest rap song on the platform to accumulate 100 million (9 days),[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-71) 200 million (19 days),[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-72) 300 million (35 days),[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-73) 400 million (54 days),[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-74) 500 million (70 days),[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-75) 600 million (87 days),[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-:0-69) and 700 million streams (112 days).[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-76) It accumulated one billion streams in mid-January 2025.[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-77)
### United States
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Not_Like_Us&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: United States")]
In the United States, "Not Like Us" debuted at number one on the [_Billboard_ Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Hot_100 "Billboard Hot 100") chart dated May 18, 2024, opening with 70.9 million streams, five million radio airplay audience impressions, and 15,000 copies sold. It registered the highest first-week streaming figure for a hip hop song since _Billboard_ removed YouTube song user-generated content from its chart metrics in 2020. As Lamar's fourth number-one single and first solo number-one debut, "Not Like Us" became the first rap song in history to top the Hot 100 with a shortened tracking week of five days.[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-Hot_100-78) It also marked Mustard's first number-one single and debut as a producer, and one of the only chart leaders to be penned by a sole writer.[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-79)
Following its music video premiere,[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-80) "Not Like Us" bested "[A Bar Song (Tipsy)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_Bar_Song_\(Tipsy\) "A Bar Song \(Tipsy\)")" by [Shaboozey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shaboozey "Shaboozey") and returned to number one on the Hot 100 chart, dated July 20, 2024, with 53.8 million streams, 40 million radio airplay audience impressions, and 8,000 copies sold. It is the longest-running solo chart-topper of Lamar's career, surpassing "[Humble](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Humble_\(song\) "Humble \(song\)")".[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-81) In October 2024, "Not Like Us" broke the record set by "[Old Town Road](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Old_Town_Road "Old Town Road")" by [Lil Nas X](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Nas_X "Lil Nas X") featuring [Billy Ray Cyrus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billy_Ray_Cyrus "Billy Ray Cyrus") for the most weeks spent atop the [Hot Rap Songs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hot_Rap_Songs "Hot Rap Songs") chart.[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-82) It's also the second longest-charting number-one song on the [Hot R&B/Hip-Hop Songs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hot_R&B/Hip-Hop_Songs "Hot R&B/Hip-Hop Songs") chart.[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-83) By the end of the year, "Not Like Us", accumulated 823.5 million on-demand audio streams in the US, making it the second most streamed song of the year and was the sixth best-performing song on the _Billboard_ Hot 100 in 2024.[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-84)[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-85) Just after Lamar's performance at the Super Bowl LIX halftime show, the song once again returned to number one on the Hot 100 chart, dated February 22, 2025 (with 49 million streams, 20.5 million radio airplay audience impressions, and 33,000 copies sold), becoming the third-longest break between time at number one in the chart's history, and the first non-holiday song to top the Hot 100 three separate times with breaks of two or more months between times at number one.[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-86) The song also charted at number thirteen on [Pop Airplay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pop_Airplay "Pop Airplay")[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-billboardpop-87) and topped the [Rhythmic Airplay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhythmic_Airplay "Rhythmic Airplay") charts.[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-rhythmic-88) On July 8, 2025, _[Complex](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Complex_\(magazine\) "Complex \(magazine\)")_ reported that the song has sold over 10 million copies in the United States.[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-ColeB-89)
### United Kingdom and Oceania
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Not_Like_Us&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: United Kingdom and Oceania")]
In the United Kingdom, "Not Like Us" debuted at number ten on the [UK Singles Chart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UK_singles_chart "UK singles chart"), and initially peaked at number six, becoming Lamar's eighth top ten hit song in Britain,[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-90) as well as topping the [Hip Hop/R&B](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UK_Hip_Hop_and_R&B_Singles_and_Albums_Charts "UK Hip Hop and R&B Singles and Albums Charts") chart.[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-ukrandb-91) Following Lamar's performance at the [Super Bowl LIX halftime show](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_LIX_halftime_show "Super Bowl LIX halftime show"), the song peaked at #1 on February 21, 2025, becoming his first chart-topping song on the UK Singles Chart. It remained atop the chart for two weeks.[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-92)
In New Zealand, "Not Like Us" debuted at number six on the [Official Aotearoa Music Charts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Official_Aotearoa_Music_Charts "Official Aotearoa Music Charts") dated May 13, 2024. Two weeks later, it reached number two for one week before dropping out of the top three. Following its music video release, "Not Like Us" became Lamar's second number-one single as a solo artist, and his third overall in the country. It remained atop for another week.[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-93)
In Australia, "Not Like Us" debuted at number nine on the [ARIA Charts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ARIA_Charts "ARIA Charts") dated May 19, 2024. It reached number five the following week, at its initial peak. The song reached number five for its second week after the release of the music video, dated July 21, 2024.[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-94) On the week of February 17, 2025, following his [Grammy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/67th_Annual_Grammy_Awards "67th Annual Grammy Awards") wins and performance at the Super Bowl LIX halftime show, "Not Like Us" reached number one, becoming Lamar's first number-one hit as a solo artist.[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-95) It also topped the Hip Hop/R&B chart.[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-australiahiphop-96)
Following his performances at the Super Bowl LIX halftime show, the song debuted at number 52 on the [Brasil Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brasil_Hot_100 "Brasil Hot 100"),[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-97) and at number 86 on the [Japan Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Japan_Hot_100 "Billboard Japan Hot 100"),[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-98) becoming his first entries on both charts.

### Synopsis
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Not_Like_Us&action=edit&section=13 "Edit section: Synopsis")]
The video starts with a view of the Compton Courthouse overlooking the [Martin Luther King, Jr. Memorial](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martin_Luther_King,_Jr._Memorial_\(Compton\) "Martin Luther King, Jr. Memorial \(Compton\)"). Lamar sashays down a white, [morgue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morgue "Morgue")-like hall to a snippet of the then-unreleased song "[Squabble Up](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Squabble_Up "Squabble Up")" from his sixth studio album, _[GNX](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GNX_\(album\) "GNX \(album\)")_ (2024). Upon knocking on a door using the "[Shave and a Haircut](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shave_and_a_Haircut "Shave and a Haircut")" tune, [Tommy the Clown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tommy_the_Clown "Tommy the Clown") slides open an eye hole and asks for the password. Lamar whispers the code, "I see dead people", and is allowed entry,[[111]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-EWMV-111) although he is scolded for being late. He takes his seat with his classmates, the Hip Hop Clowns, and grooves to "Not Like Us". Lamar gives [the finger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_finger "The finger") and dances in the corner. A classmate passes him a [Bible](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bible "Bible"), which he carefully slips in his jacket.
Using [cinematography](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cinematography "Cinematography") that mirrors the lyric video for "[Family Matters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Family_Matters_\(Drake_song\) "Family Matters \(Drake song\)")",[[129]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-Price-129) a covered figure resembling Drake on the cover of _[Dark Lane Demo Tapes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dark_Lane_Demo_Tapes "Dark Lane Demo Tapes")_ (2020) tries to ambush Lamar from behind; he is quickly blown away.[[129]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-Price-129) Lamar completes seventeen (not 18) [push-ups](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Push-up "Push-up") on four [cinder blocks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Concrete_block "Concrete block")—a response to Drake ordering him to "drop and give me fifty" on "[Push Ups](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Push_Ups_\(song\) "Push Ups \(song\)")"—in a bedroom with strong similarities to a [prison cell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prison_cell "Prison cell"). He then strikes an owl-shaped [piñata](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pi%C3%B1ata "Piñata") and glides down a [hopscotch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hopscotch "Hopscotch") court numbered 1 through 10. A [disclaimer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disclaimer "Disclaimer") insulting Drake's record label, [OVO Sound](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/OVO_Sound "OVO Sound"), is shown as he repeatedly hits the piñata.[[130]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-130) [Aerial shots](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aerial_photography "Aerial photography") of a large crowd of Compton residents gathered inside of the memorial and chanting the song are featured throughout the video.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]
Lamar and Mustard take a drive through Compton's [Rosecrans Avenue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosecrans_Avenue "Rosecrans Avenue") in a black [Ferrari SF90 Stradale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferrari_SF90_Stradale "Ferrari SF90 Stradale"). They stop at [Tam's Burgers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tam's_Burgers "Tam's Burgers") #21 to grab some food with dancer Storm DeBarge. Lamar then joins a group of friends on a rooftop near the Courthouse before meeting Free and [DeMar DeRozan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DeMar_DeRozan "DeMar DeRozan") at a [dockyard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shipyard "Shipyard") containing white shipping containers. Dancers [Kida the Great](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kida_Burns "Kida Burns") and Taiwan Williams accompany Lamar on the dockyard, while La'Donna is seen [tightrope walking](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tightrope_walking "Tightrope walking") in the clouds.[[131]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-131)[[132]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-132) At [Nickerson Gardens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nickerson_Gardens "Nickerson Gardens"), Lamar hangs out with his former [Top Dawg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Top_Dawg_Entertainment "Top Dawg Entertainment") labelmates [Jay Rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jay_Rock "Jay Rock"), [Schoolboy Q](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Schoolboy_Q "Schoolboy Q") and [Ab-Soul](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ab-Soul "Ab-Soul") (collectively known as [Black Hippy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Hippy "Black Hippy")), along with executives Anthony "Top Dawg" Tiffith, [Terrence "Punch" Henderson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Punch_\(rapper\) "Punch \(rapper\)"), and Anthony "Moosa" Tiffith Jr.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]
Shifting back to the classroom, Lamar and the Hip Hop Clowns perform a [number](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Number_\(music\) "Number \(music\)") under Tommy the Clown's watch. Lamar poses with his partner Whitney Alford and their children in a [living room](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Living_room "Living room"); the couple dances joyfully while the children play.[[122]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-Decode-122) A [barn owl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barn-owl "Barn-owl") and Lamar engage in a stare down—as he leaves, the owl realizes it has been locked in a cage.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] In what appears to be unedited footage from the shoot, Free asks the rapturous Compton crowd through a [bullhorn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Megaphone "Megaphone") if they want to play the song again as the [end titles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Closing_credits "Closing credits") appear on the screen.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]
### Reception and analysis
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Not_Like_Us&action=edit&section=14 "Edit section: Reception and analysis")]
The music video was met with widespread critical acclaim. Numerous publications and websites called it another victory lap for Lamar in his feud with Drake.[[a]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-138) [CBC News](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CBC_News "CBC News") called it a moment of re-ignition of the feud,[[138]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-139) while _[Vibe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vibe_\(magazine\) "Vibe \(magazine\)")_ opined it as Lamar's "knockout punch" against Drake.[[139]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-VIBEMV-140) Journalists described the video as refuting Drake's allegations against Lamar: it depicts Lamar's family dancing happily alongside him,[[111]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-EWMV-111)[[112]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-GQMV-112) and the video credits emphasize Lamar and Free's collaboration.[[111]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-EWMV-111)[[140]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-UPMV-141)
[Vinson Cunningham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vinson_Cunningham "Vinson Cunningham") of _[The New Yorker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_New_Yorker "The New Yorker")_ thought that the video's Independence Day release was a "[jingoistic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jingoism "Jingoism") move" that draws a "bright line" along the [Canada–United States border](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canada%E2%80%93United_States_border "Canada–United States border"). He made an "[Edenic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garden_of_Eden "Garden of Eden")" comparison to the image of Lamar and his family posing with [Grant Wood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grant_Wood "Grant Wood")'s _[American Gothic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Gothic "American Gothic")_ (1930) and [Gordon Parks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gordon_Parks "Gordon Parks")'s [1942 photograph of the same name](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Gothic_\(photograph\) "American Gothic \(photograph\)"), arguing that the frame inaugurated a "new sort" of [American iconography](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Culture_of_the_United_States "Culture of the United States").[[141]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-Cunningham-142) _[Entertainment Weekly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Entertainment_Weekly "Entertainment Weekly")_ observed the inclusion of new music in the intro to the video, noting fan speculation that it was to be included in Lamar's potential next studio album.[[111]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-EWMV-111) _[USA Today](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USA_Today "USA Today")_ 's Naledi Ushe mused that with the release of the music video, Lamar had aimed to take Drake's "song of the summer trophy", noting Drake's perceived achievement with several of his late 2010s singles and the relative failure of the singles from _[For All the Dogs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_All_the_Dogs "For All the Dogs")_ (2023), leaving the title open for Lamar and [Sabrina Carpenter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sabrina_Carpenter "Sabrina Carpenter") with "[Espresso](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Espresso_\(song\) "Espresso \(song\)")" to contend.[[142]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-143) [NBC News](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBC_News "NBC News") noted the song's appraisal as a celebration of Compton and the West Coast.[[120]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-NBCMV-120) _[GQ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GQ "GQ")_ appreciated Lamar's choice of [fashion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fashion "Fashion") style in the video, pointing out that his wearing of a [Prada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prada "Prada") suit and multiple [Martine Rose](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martine_Rose "Martine Rose") track jackets reinforced a [claim](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Hillbillies "The Hillbillies") that he made a year ago that he "is the best-dressed MC in rap".[[143]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-GQFSHNMV-144)
## Drake's response
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Not_Like_Us&action=edit&section=15 "Edit section: Drake's response")]
Drake responded with "[The Heart Part 6](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Heart_Part_6 "The Heart Part 6")" one day after "Not Like Us" was released,[[144]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-145) in which he denied all accusations and stated that he would have liked to dance to "Not Like Us" if Lamar was not "tripling down on some whole other bullshit".[[145]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-146) On November 24, 2024, Drake appeared on a [Kick](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kick_\(service\) "Kick \(service\)") [livestream](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live_streaming "Live streaming") with Canadian streamer [xQc](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/XQc "XQc"), describing himself as "fully intact, mind, body, and soul". Lamar reacted to these comments with amusement.[[146]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-147)[[147]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-148)
### Legal actions
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Not_Like_Us&action=edit&section=16 "Edit section: Legal actions")]
On November 25, 2024, Drake filed a petition against [Universal Music Group](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Universal_Music_Group "Universal Music Group") (UMG) and Spotify under [New York law](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Law_of_New_York_\(state\) "Law of New York \(state\)") claiming that they had conspired to artificially inflate the popularity of "Not Like Us" to "deceive consumers into believing the song was more popular than it was in reality". His attorneys accused UMG of violating the [Racketeer Influenced and Corrupt Organizations Act](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Racketeer_Influenced_and_Corrupt_Organizations_Act "Racketeer Influenced and Corrupt Organizations Act") (RICO) and using deceptive business practices and false advertising.[[148]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-149) UMG stated in response that the allegations were "offensive and untrue", that they would "never do anything to undermine" any artist signed to the label, and that "fans choose the music they want to hear".[[149]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-150)[[150]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-151) Drake later filed a second petition against UMG under [Texas law](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Law_of_Texas "Law of Texas") claiming [defamation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Defamation "Defamation") by failing to halt the release of a song "falsely accusing him of being a sex offender." He also accused UMG of "funneling payments" to [iHeartRadio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IHeartRadio "IHeartRadio") as part of a "[pay-to-play](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pay-to-play "Pay-to-play") scheme" to promote "Not Like Us" on the radio.[[151]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-152)
On January 15, 2025, Drake filed a defamation lawsuit in [New York federal court](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_District_Court_for_the_Southern_District_of_New_York "United States District Court for the Southern District of New York") against UMG, with substantially the same factual allegations. He did not include Lamar as a defendant.[[152]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-153) In March, UMG moved to dismiss the lawsuit, arguing that Drake "lost a rap battle that he provoked and in which he willingly participated," and that he should have "accept[ed] the loss like the unbothered rap artist he often claims to be."[[153]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-154) The case was assigned to Judge [Jeannette Vargas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeannette_Vargas "Jeannette Vargas"), who allowed Drake's legal team to subpoena Kojo Menne Asamoah, a potential witness.[[154]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-155) On October 9, 2025, Vargas dismissed the suit.[[155]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-156) She held that New York law did not permit [defamation lawsuits for statements of opinion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_defamation_law#Opinion_Privilege "United States defamation law"). She concluded that a reasonable listener would understand that rap battles are opinionated and that diss tracks are not "fact-checked verifiable content."[[156]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-157) Drake [appealed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Appeal "Appeal") on October 29.[[157]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-158) A court hearing for the appeal is set for December 4, 2026.[[158]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-159)
## Notable live performances
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Not_Like_Us&action=edit&section=17 "Edit section: Notable live performances")]
### The Pop Out: Ken & Friends
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Not_Like_Us&action=edit&section=18 "Edit section: The Pop Out: Ken & Friends")]
Further information: [The Pop Out: Ken & Friends § "Not Like Us" performances](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Pop_Out:_Ken_&_Friends#"Not_Like_Us"_performances "The Pop Out: Ken & Friends")
During [the Pop Out: Ken & Friends](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Pop_Out:_Ken_&_Friends "The Pop Out: Ken & Friends"), held on [Juneteenth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juneteenth "Juneteenth") 2024 at the [Kia Forum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kia_Forum "Kia Forum") in [Inglewood, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inglewood,_California "Inglewood, California"), Lamar performed "Not Like Us" for the first time.[[159]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-160) The song was introduced by [Dr. Dre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dr._Dre "Dr. Dre") whispering the opening lines. The track was followed by four consecutive reprises,[[160]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-161) the last two featured a wide assortment of emerging and notable West Coast figures.[[161]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-162)[[162]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-Rolling-2024-6-19-163) [NPR Music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NPR_Music "NPR Music")'s Sheldon Pearce compared the picture to [Art Kane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Art_Kane "Art Kane")'s _[A Great Day in Harlem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_Great_Day_in_Harlem "A Great Day in Harlem")_ (1958).[[163]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-164) Several critics viewed the "raw" performances of "Not Like Us" as a highlight of the concert and praised its liveliness.[[164]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-165) David Dennis Jr. of _[Andscape](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andscape "Andscape")_ commended the way Lamar turned a song centered on his disdain for Drake into a moment of "unity and love".[[165]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-166)
### Super Bowl LIX halftime show
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Not_Like_Us&action=edit&section=19 "Edit section: Super Bowl LIX halftime show")]
See also: [Super Bowl LIX halftime show](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_LIX_halftime_show "Super Bowl LIX halftime show")
On September 8, 2024, Lamar was announced as the headlining act for the [Super Bowl LIX halftime show](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_LIX_halftime_show "Super Bowl LIX halftime show") at the [Caesars Superdome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caesars_Superdome "Caesars Superdome") in [New Orleans, Louisiana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Orleans "New Orleans").[[166]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-167) Speculation arose as to whether he would incorporate "Not Like Us" into his performance.[[167]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-168)[[168]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-169) Justin Sayles of _[The Ringer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Ringer_\(website\) "The Ringer \(website\)")_ called the halftime performance announcement as the capstone of a year that had seen Lamar "ascend to the highest levels" of popular culture, and seen Drake "sink to the lowest levels" of his career.[[169]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-Sayles-170)
"Not Like Us" would indeed be performed towards the end of Lamar's Super Bowl halftime setlist on February 9, 2025. In an interlude during the middle of the set, Lamar teased the song and alluded to Drake's litigation by quipping "I want to perform their favorite song, but you know they love to sue", which was followed by a brief audio clip of the song's introduction.[[170]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-171) In another interlude after performing "[All the Stars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All_the_Stars "All the Stars")", he said "they tried to rig the game but you can't fake influence", then launched into "Not Like Us".[[171]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-172) Lamar looked directly into the camera with a smile when he rapped "Say Drake, I hear you like 'em young". The lyric including the word "pedophile" was censored, but the audience could be heard shouting the lyric "tryna strike a chord and it's probably A minor" along with him a few lines later.[[172]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-CNNDrake-173)[[173]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-174)
Professional tennis player [Serena Williams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Serena_Williams "Serena Williams"), who shares Lamar's hometown of Compton, made a cameo appearance as a dancer doing a [crip walk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crip_Walk "Crip Walk") during "Not Like Us",[[174]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-Guests-175)[[175]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-176) a reference to Williams performing a similar dance after her victory at the [2012 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tennis_at_the_2012_Summer_Olympics_%E2%80%93_Women's_singles "Tennis at the 2012 Summer Olympics – Women's singles"), for which she faced some criticism. Williams's appearance was also received as a diss towards Drake, with whom she was rumored to have dated several years earlier.[[176]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-177)[[177]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-178)[[178]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-179)
Lisa Respers France of [CNN](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CNN "CNN") would call "Not Like Us" the star of the halftime performance, while Maria Sherman of the [Associated Press](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Associated_Press "Associated Press") described Lamar performing the song on the biggest stage in US sports, especially days after the song swept the Grammy Awards, as "another step in Lamar's continued victory lap".[[172]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-CNNDrake-173)[[179]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-180)
## Cultural impact
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Not_Like_Us&action=edit&section=20 "Edit section: Cultural impact")]
### Economy and fashion
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Not_Like_Us&action=edit&section=21 "Edit section: Economy and fashion")]
Following the release of the music video for "Not Like Us", [Tam's Burgers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tam's_Burgers "Tam's Burgers") #21 saw a significant spike in business.[[180]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-181) Lauro Hernandez and his son Bryan Noe, the managers of the restaurant, reported that they experienced a 30% to 40% boost in sales.[[181]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-182) Spiro Vovos, who owns the Tam's Burgers chain, later clarified that it was more of a surge in foot traffic and [content creators](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Content_creation "Content creation") visiting the location; the sales influx mostly occurred as the video was being filmed.[[182]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-183) A [mural](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mural "Mural") honoring Lamar and "Not Like Us" was painted on the restaurant's exterior by Mike Norice.[[183]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-184)[[184]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-185) Fashion brands such as [Willy Chavarria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willy_Chavarria "Willy Chavarria") also enjoyed substantial increases in brand recognition and sales after their pieces were featured in the music video.[[185]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-186)
[Small business owners](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Small_business "Small business") in Compton, however, were negatively impacted by the production of the music video.[[186]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-187) In a report conducted by the _[Los Angeles Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles_Times "Los Angeles Times")_ , a [strip mall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Strip_mall "Strip mall") across from the Compton Courthouse that houses local businesses had its parking lot overrun by "cars and chaos" as hundreds of people poured out to the Courthouse to catch a glimpse of Lamar. The mall's owners had to shut down operations and claimed they lost thousands of dollars during the shoot. They placed the blame on city officials for their lack of communication, and have asked Lamar, PGLang, or the city government to provide [financial compensation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Financial_compensation "Financial compensation").[[187]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-188)

Henson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taraji_P._Henson "Taraji P. Henson") [parodied](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parody_music "Parody music") "Not Like Us" as part of her opening monologue.[[196]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-197) Serena Williams [crip walked](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crip_Walk "Crip Walk") to the track while hosting the [2024 ESPY Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_ESPY_Awards "2024 ESPY Awards").[[197]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-198) [Richie Branson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richie_Branson "Richie Branson") composed a [chiptune](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chiptune "Chiptune") version of the track and designed a free-to-play [video game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Video_game "Video game"), titled _Not Like Us: The Game_.[[198]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-199)[[199]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-200) It attracted 1.2 million players during the first 36 hours of its release.[[200]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-201)[[201]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-202) Some [iPhone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IPhone "IPhone") users noticed that if they asked [Siri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Siri "Siri") to play Drake's _[Certified Lover Boy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Certified_Lover_Boy "Certified Lover Boy")_ (2021) on Spotify, it would occasionally play "Not Like Us" instead.[[202]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-203) The song was added into [Beat Saber](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beat_Saber "Beat Saber") as DLC.[[203]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-204) [Conan O'Brien](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conan_O'Brien "Conan O'Brien") made reference to the song while telling a joke about Drake at the [Academy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Awards "Academy Awards").[[204]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-205)
### Politics
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Not_Like_Us&action=edit&section=23 "Edit section: Politics")]
"Not Like Us" was referenced a number of times during the [2024 US election cycle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_United_States_elections "2024 United States elections"). [Democratic Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Democratic_Party_\(United_States\) "Democratic Party \(United States\)") figures including vice president [Kamala Harris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kamala_Harris "Kamala Harris"),[[205]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-206) representative [Jasmine Crockett](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jasmine_Crockett "Jasmine Crockett"),[[206]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-207) mayor of Baltimore [Brandon Scott](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brandon_Scott "Brandon Scott"),[[207]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-208) attorney general of Illinois [Kwame Raoul](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kwame_Raoul "Kwame Raoul"),[[208]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-209) and a [protest against Donald Trump](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protests_against_Donald_Trump "Protests against Donald Trump") in Chicago used the song's chorus as a political metaphor to criticize Trump and members of the [Republican Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republican_Party_\(United_States\) "Republican Party \(United States\)").[[209]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-210)[[210]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-211)[[211]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-212) Sports journalist [Bomani Jones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bomani_Jones "Bomani Jones") argued that the song influenced a shift in campaign messaging on "every side",[[212]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-:1-213) suggesting a parallel with politicians like [Tim Walz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tim_Walz "Tim Walz"), the governor of Minnesota, publicly branding Trump, his [running mate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Running_mate "Running mate") [JD Vance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/JD_Vance "JD Vance"), and other Republicans as "weird".[[212]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-:1-213)[[213]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-214)
After incumbent president [Joe Biden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Biden "Joe Biden") [withdrew](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Withdrawal_of_Joe_Biden_from_the_2024_United_States_presidential_election "Withdrawal of Joe Biden from the 2024 United States presidential election") from the [2024 presidential election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_United_States_presidential_election "2024 United States presidential election"), Harris incorporated "Not Like Us" into [her own presidential campaign](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kamala_Harris_2024_presidential_campaign "Kamala Harris 2024 presidential campaign") with Walz as her running mate.[[214]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-215)[[215]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-216) Journalists were intrigued by the decision, as Harris's [mixed-race ancestry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Family_of_Kamala_Harris#Ancestry_of_Kamala_Harris "Family of Kamala Harris") was a subject of questioning by her opponents,[[216]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-217) while younger supporters such as Parker Short were energized by it.[[217]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-218)[[218]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-219) During the [2024 Democratic National Convention](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Democratic_National_Convention "2024 Democratic National Convention"), "Not Like Us" was chosen as one of the four walk-on songs to represent California at the ceremonial roll call.[[219]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-220)[[220]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-221) It was referenced by Alabama congressional candidate [Shomari Figures](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shomari_Figures "Shomari Figures") in the context of [voting rights](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Voting_rights_in_the_United_States "Voting rights in the United States") during his address at the convention.[[221]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-222) The Democratic Party referenced the song's cover artwork to criticize Donald Trump's relationship with child sex trafficker [Jeffrey Epstein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeffrey_Epstein "Jeffrey Epstein") and his refusal to declassify [files](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Epstein_files "Epstein files") related to the case.[[222]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-223) In [global politics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Global_politics "Global politics"), rapper Sabi Wu sampled "Not Like Us" to compose a [protest song](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protest_song "Protest song") [opposing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya_Finance_Bill_protests "Kenya Finance Bill protests") the [Kenya Finance Bill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya_Finance_Bill_2024 "Kenya Finance Bill 2024").[[223]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-224)

### Crime
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Not_Like_Us&action=edit&section=25 "Edit section: Crime")]
Drake's OVO clothing retailer on [London](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/London "London")'s [Carnaby Street](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carnaby_Street "Carnaby Street") was [vandalized](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vandalism "Vandalism") on May 7, 2024, by an unknown [graffiti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Graffiti "Graffiti") artist, who plastered the phrase "They not like us" in silver lettering on its window.[[233]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-234) The [Metropolitan Police](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metropolitan_Police "Metropolitan Police") did not announce plans to investigate the store tagging and no arrests were made.[[234]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-235) In the following days, two separate individuals were apprehended by the [Toronto Police](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toronto_Police_Service "Toronto Police Service") while attempting to break into Drake's [Bridle Path](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bridle_Path,_Toronto "Bridle Path, Toronto") home; the same residence shown on the cover art for "Not Like Us".[[235]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-236) On June 30, 2024, [Rick Ross](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Ross "Rick Ross") and his entourage were attacked at the Ignite Music Festival in [Vancouver](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vancouver "Vancouver"), Canada, by a group of attendees after he played "Not Like Us" to close out his headlining set.[[236]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-237) Ross later reported to TMZ that no one from his team suffered any serious injuries from the assault.[[237]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us#cite_note-238)
